International Admissions
Proof of English Proficiency
Requirements
All applicants, regardless of citizenship, must provide proof of English proficiency to be considered for admission to Marshall University. All English proficiency requirements are listed below. If one or more of the exemption conditions is met, applicants may be considered exempt from providing standardized exam scores for proof of English proficiency.

Exemptions
If one of the following criteria are met, exam scores will not be required, and the proof of English proficiency requirement will be met:
All Applicants
Completion of the equivalent to a United States post-secondary degree from an accepted, accredited institution in an approved country where the primary language is English. (See list below.)
One year of full-time study (24 Undergraduate or 18 Graduate credit hours) earned at a United States-accepted and accredited university.
Transfer credit equivalent to ENG 101 from an accepted, accredited institution with grade of C or better.
Successful completion of an approved ESL program.
Undergraduate Applicants Only
Completion of the equivalent to a United States high school diploma from an accepted, accredited institution in an approved country where the primary language is English. (See list below.)
One year of study at a United States high school, with a C or higher in English
Earned a C or higher on the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) or O-Level English First Language subject exam from Cambridge Assessment International
Passed full year of IB English Language & Literature or IB English A with IBDP1 HL with 4 or higher, SL with 5 or higher (not English B)
Approved List of Countries for Direct Entry English Proficiency Exemption
The proof of English proficiency requirement may be waived if we receive official proof of the equivalent of a U.S. high school diploma or U.S. post-secondary degree from an accepted, accredited institution in one of the approved English-speaking countries listed below.
This list is determined at the sole discretion of Marshall University and is subject to change without prior notice.
